summary: This configuration block sets up error handling for PHP by enabling error display and logging. It tells the web server to show errors to users, log them to a file, and track which errors occurred—but only if the PHP 5 module is actually installed and active on the server.

explanations.1: This checks whether the Apache server has the mod_php5 module loaded; everything between this tag and </IfModule> only runs if it does.
explanations.2: This tells PHP to display error messages directly in the browser output, which is helpful for debugging but should usually be turned off in production.
explanations.4: This makes PHP remember the last error that occurred so you can retrieve it later, which is useful for custom error handling.
explanations.5: This specifies that PHP errors should be written to a file called 'error.log' instead of (or in addition to) being displayed.
